title: Hearts and Rangers: Naderi's Tangled Trail Tells Us Little Yet
body:
Sky Sports reports that Derek McInnes has revealed Hearts were interested in Ryan Naderi before Rangers moved in, and that a new deal was being discussed [S1]. When two sides chase the same player, the paperwork gets messy and the rumours multiply.

McInnes hoped the signing would fall through ten months earlier [S1]. That is a striking admission, and it shows how long this story has been simmering. BBC Sport, meanwhile, framed Naderi's contribution as a "lucky punch" that kept Rangers in touch on a Saturday full of Scottish Premiership goals [S2].

The on-pitch evidence is thin. By BBC's account, Naderi's moment was far from the most impressive of the day, yet it still mattered [S2]. One decisive moment is not a body of work, and it should not settle a debate about a player's future or a club's judgement of him.

The smart money is on patience. Fans love a bidding war and a rival's regret, but those are sideshows to what the player delivers over a season.

The Touchline Take: judge the business when the window shuts, not before.

evidence.text: Sky Sports: McInnes reveals Hearts Naderi interest before Rangers move as new deal discussed. Derek McInnes hoped the signing of Ryan Naderi would fall through 10 months ago.
BBC Sport: Naderi's 'lucky punch' keeps Rangers in touch. On a Saturday laden with Scottish Premiership goals, Ryan Naderi's was far from the most impressive - but vital for Rangers all the same.
